result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers reframe 'validate' around a build, pilot or drop decision, and both put past-behavior interviews and existing data ahead of a survey. A is better because it is more proportionate. It keeps the fake door optional and depends on engineering and VP approval. It also states plainly what the tickets can show and what only interviews can, and it lists the steps a human must do. B commits to a fake-door test in week 2 that may not fit the time or resources. B's best point is asking which kind of insurance the VP means, and it also states the limits of the evidence clearly. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B names the decision (build, pilot or drop) and explains why a small study is enough. It separates what support tickets and booking data can show from what only interviews can, says what would shift the recommendation, and lists the steps a person must do. A is solid and practical too, but it is less clear about who does what, and it slots a fake-door test into week 2 without noting that it needs engineering time and the VP's approval.
